What We Do

Full-Service General Surgery Revenue Cycle Management

General surgery billing requires precise operative report coding, global period tracking, and modifier compliance across hundreds of procedure codes. PMEX reviews every operative report before coding and manages the full claim lifecycle from submission to payment.

Operative Report Coding

Surgical CPT codes selected from the operative report, not from superbill defaults.

Global Period Tracking

10-day and 90-day global periods tracked per surgeon per procedure.

Assistant Surgeon Billing

Modifier 80, 81, and 82 applied when assistant documentation supports separate billing.

Multiple Procedure Reduction

Modifier 51 applied correctly when multiple procedures performed in one session.

Laparoscopic vs. Open Coding

Laparoscopic CPT codes applied when the operative report confirms approach.

Outpatient Surgery Coordination

ASC and hospital outpatient facility coordination managed per case.

Sound Familiar?

Common General Surgery Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Open procedure billed when laparoscopic approach was used, or vice versa.

PMEX reads every operative report to confirm surgical approach before selecting the CPT code.

Post-op E/M billed during global period without modifier 24 or 79.

PMEX tracks the global period per surgeon per procedure and flags every post-op visit for correct billing.

Assistant surgeon claim submitted without documentation of medical necessity for assistance.

PMEX confirms assistant surgeon documentation and payer policy before submitting modifier 80 or 82.

Anesthesia and surgeon claims not coordinated, creating duplicate service flags.

PMEX coordinates with the anesthesia team to ensure consistent procedure codes across both claims.

Modifier 51 missing on multi-procedure cases, triggering incorrect bundling.

PMEX applies modifier 51 per the correct multiple-procedure reduction rules before submission.

Unlisted procedure code used when a specific CPT code exists for the procedure.

PMEX matches every procedure to the most specific billable CPT code before falling back to an unlisted code.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in General Surgery Billing

General surgery practices lose 14 to 22 percent of revenue to operative report coding errors, global period violations, and bundling mistakes.

PATTERN 01

Laparoscopic Procedure Billed as Open

Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (47562) performed. Billing team submits open cholecystectomy (47600, higher RVU). Payer audits operative report. Finds laparoscopic approach. Recoups the difference. Compliance exposure created.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes every surgery from the operative report approach confirmation. Laparoscopic vs. open is verified before CPT selection on every case.

PATTERN 02

Post-Op Visit Billed During Global Period

Patient presents 3 weeks after appendectomy (90-day global). Standard E/M (99213) submitted. Payer denies as included in the global surgical fee. $85 lost per visit without modifier 24 (new condition) or modifier 79 (unrelated procedure).

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks the global period end date for every surgical patient and routes post-op visits to the correct billing path: included in global, modifier 24 for new conditions, or modifier 79 for unrelated procedures.

PATTERN 03

Multiple Procedures Bundled Incorrectly

Cholecystectomy and hernia repair performed in the same session. Both billed at full fee. Payer applies multiple procedure reduction. Modifier 51 was missing on the secondary procedure, creating an edit flag and manual review delay.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies modifier 51 to the secondary procedure per CMS multiple procedure reduction rules. Primary procedure identified by highest RVU value. Secondary procedures reduced at the correct percentage.

Questions

General Surgery Billing Questions Answered

The global period is 10 days (minor procedures) or 90 days (major procedures) during which routine pre-op and post-op care are included in the surgical fee. E/M visits for the same condition during this period are not separately billable.

We identify all procedures from the operative report, assign CPT codes by RVU value, apply modifier 51 to secondary procedures per CMS rules, and confirm CCI edit compatibility before submission.

Yes, when the operative report and the payer policy support it. We apply modifier 80 (assistant surgeon), 81 (minimum assistance), or 82 (qualified non-physician assistant) based on who assisted and the payer contract.

When a laparoscopic case is converted to open mid-procedure, we code the open procedure CPT with a note in the claim reflecting the conversion, per the operative report documentation.

We manage the surgeon professional fee claim. We can coordinate with the facility billing team to ensure consistent procedure codes on both the facility and professional claims.

Within 30 days, with no gap in cash flow during transition.
